This document describes the design of the Rust library and of the individual CLI
commands, as well as tracks the implementation status. This document is split
into the functions for the CLI and the library implementing the CLI.

{{< include /docs/includes/_design-status.qmd >}}

The shapes, fill colours, and bolding of the boxes in the diagrams below have
specific meanings.

- All parallelograms are all input or output.
- Light gray parallelograms with bold edges are input arguments.
- Rectangular boxes are actions or processes, such as a function.
- Cylindrical boxes are internal types, such as Rust structs.
- Diamond boxes are decision points that represent "if" conditions.

## CLI code

All the CLI functions take one argument: `args`. The type of the `args` depends
on the function name, but their struct type is always the function name with
`Args` as the suffix (e.g. `ListArgs`). These structs are created when Rust
parses the command when it is used on the CLI. The output of these CLI functions
is typical Rust types (e.g. `Result`), however, when used within `main()` after
parsing the CLI args, they get converted to pretty printed stdout.

Many internal functions or methods return a `Result` type. In those cases, the
design diagrams assume that the error will contain the correct message and be
send to `stderr`. So arrows and boxes are not included for errors to simplify
the diagrams.

The `init` CLI command isn't shown here as it is a very simple command to create
a `.zenodo.toml` file with empty `Metadata` fields.

### {{< var wip >}} `discard()` {#cli-discard}

This relatively simple function, like [`get()`](#cli-get), has an internal
`discard_deposit()` method that is used in other CLI functions. However, unlike
`get_deposit()` that requires a bit more steps, the [discard Zenodo
API](https://developers.zenodo.org/#discard) request used in `discard_deposit()`
is a (mostly) simple `POST` request to the `discard` endpoint.

```{mermaid}

    session[("Session::new()")]

    metadata[("Metadata {...}")]

    output[/"Message<br>or nothing<br>(stdout)"/]

    metadata_path -->

    decision_draft -->|false| output

```

### {{< var wip >}} `publish()` {#cli-publish}

The meaning of `--draft` compared to `--yes` has a difference and results in
different outcomes. Making a draft with `--draft` means the user wants to view
the deposit on Zenodo to confirm things before publishing. `--yes` is a flag
that tells `update()` to publish without prompting for a confirmation, which
doesn't mean anything when used with `--draft` (though nothing will happen if
both are used together). This is mainly to ensure that a command wasn't ran
accidentally.

While `is_draft()` is a `bool`, in the `true` case we output an error to
`stderr` since we don't want to modify a deposit that is in the editable state.

```{mermaid}

%%|   document.

flowchart TD

    yes[/"--yes"/]:::inputs
    sandbox[/"--sandbox"/]:::inputs
    metadata_file[/"[metadata-file]"/]:::inputs
    files[/"--file"/]:::inputs

    token["get_token()"]
    session[("Session::new()")]
    confirm_publish["confirm_publish()"]
    read_metadata["read_metadata()"]
    metadata[("Metadata {...}")]
    session_without_files[("Session {...}<br>Without files")]
    create_deposit["create_deposit()"]
    is_draft["is_draft()"]
    create_new_version["create_new_version()"]
    add_files["add_files()"]
    delete_files["delete_files()"]
    update_deposit["update_deposit()"]
    publish["publish_deposit()"]
    discard_deposit["discard_deposit()"]
    output[/"Deposit<br>or nothing"/]

    decision_publish{"publish?"}
    decision_draft{"draft?"}
    decision_editable{"editable?"}
    decision_has_deposit{"has deposit?"}

    sandbox --> token
    sandbox & token -->
      session

    draft -->
      decision_draft -->|true| output

    files --> add_files

    session -->
      decision_has_deposit -->|Some| is_draft -->
      decision_editable -->|false| create_new_version

    decision_has_deposit -->|None| create_deposit
    metadata -->
      create_deposit -->
      session_without_files

    decision_editable --> |true| error[/Error/]

    create_new_version -->
      delete_files -->
      session_without_files -->
      add_files

    add_files & metadata -->
      update_deposit -->
      decision_draft -->|false| decision_publish

    decision_publish -->|true| publish -->
      output

    metadata_file -->
      read_metadata -->

    metadata -->|add ZendoID| session

    yes -->
      confirm_publish -->
      decision_publish -->|false| discard_deposit -->

    classDef inputs fill:lightgray,stroke-width:3px
```

### {{< var wip >}} `sync()` {#cli-sync}

Because of the wide variety of potential output formats, the internals of this
function need to be flexible to adding new formats. It makes heavy use of traits
and generics in `impl` methods in Rust to keep a simple flow. Methods of the
traits are applied to each of the formats structs, e.g. for `CitationCff` or
`ZenodoJson`.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-sync-cli
%%| fig-cap: >-
%%|   The flow of input and output through the `sync()` CLI function. 'New'
%%|   metadata synced to a format is joined with the 'old' metadata in that
%%|   format.
%%| fig-alt: >-
%%|   Diagram showing the flow of input and output from input to output. There
%%|   are various shapes for each box, which is described at the top of the
%%|   document.

flowchart TD
    metadata_path[/"[metadata_path]"/]
    to[/"--to"/]

    read_metadata["read_metadata()"]
    metadata[("Metadata {...}")]
    formats[("ToFormats<br>enum")]
    sync_format["sync_format()<br>method"]
    output[/"Updated<br>format file"/]

    metadata_path -->
      read_metadata -->
      metadata -->
      sync_format

    to -->
      formats -->|match to<br>correct<br>format struct| sync_format -->
      output
```

## Library code

This section describes the non-CLI library interface, which the CLI functions
use internally use. They are higher-level descriptions, mainly here to provide
function signatures as well as some reasons for their design (if needed).

`enum ToFormats`

:   This `enum` contains a listing of all the different the different formats we
    sync to as received from the `--to` arg, as listed in the
    [CLI](cli.qmd#cli-sync) page.

`trait from(metadata: &Metadata) -> Self`

:   This uses the built-in `From` trait to build
    [`from()`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/convert/trait.From.html) `impl`
    methods on the different format structs. For example, for `CitationCff` it
    could be `impl From<&Metadata> for CitationCff`.

`Metadata {...}`

:   This contains the metadata from the Zenodo TOML file, e.g. `.zenodo.toml`.
    Will eventually form the deposit's
    [`metadata`](https://developers.zenodo.org/?shell#depositions) field.

`read_metadata(path: &Path) -> Result<Metadata, Error>`

:   Reads the Zenodo TOML file, e.g. `.zenodo.toml`.

### `sync_format()`

This generic function operates on the various format structs, e.g.
`CitationCff`. It is a simple convenience method for use in the `match` arms of
the `sync()` CLI command. It is a thin wrapper around `from()`, `read()`,
`left_join()`, and `write()`. The signature is:

```rust
fn sync_format<T>(metadata: &Metadata) -> Result<(), Error>;
```

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-sync-format
%%| fig-cap: >-
%%|   The flow of input and output through the helper `sync_format()` CLI
%%|   function. 'New' metadata synced to a format is joined with the 'old'
%%|   metadata in that format.
%%| fig-alt: >-
%%|   Diagram showing the flow of input and output from input to output. There
%%|   are various shapes for each box, which is described at the top of the
%%|   document.

flowchart TD
    metadata[("Metadata {...}")]
    from["from()<br>trait"]

    subgraph new_format ["Format structs (new)"]
      %% Fix positions with hidden arrows
      citation_cff[("CitationCff {...}")] ~~~
        pyproject_toml[("PyprojectToml {...}")]
      zenodo_json[("ZenodoJson {...}")] ~~~
        codemeta_json[("CodemetaJson {...}")]
      quarto_yml[("QuartoYml {...}")] ~~~
        description_r[("DescriptionR {...}")]
    end

    old_format[("Format structs (old)")]

    left{"left?"}
    right{"right?"}

    left_join["left_join()<br>trait"]
    read["read()<br>trait"]
    write["write()<br>trait"]

    metadata -->
      from -->
      new_format

    new_format -->
      read -->
      old_format -->
      right

    new_format -->
      left

    left & right -->
      left_join -->
      write

    new_format:::inner
    classDef inner fill:none
```

### `confirm_publish()` {#lib-confirm-publish}

The signature is:

```rust
pub fn confirm_publish(yes: bool) -> bool
```

A simple helper function to print a message confirming whether the Zenodo
deposit should be published. The value of `yes` comes from the `--yes` CLI
option and will only be the output if `yes` is given via the `--yes` flag (e.g.
is `true`).

<!-- TODO: Confirm whether response contains the deposit, then it can be added to `Deposit` -->

`Deposit {...}`

:   A struct that represents the JSON response received from Zenodo. Mainly
    needed for updating the `deposit.metadata` object and for the `deposit.id`
    fields. The Zenodo deposit fields are listed on
    [Zenodo](https://developers.zenodo.org/?shell#entities). Some fields are not
    converted from the Zenodo JSON representation to our `Deposit` struct as
    they aren't needed by zen-do nor needed during communication with the Zenodo
    API. Specifically `doi_url`, `created`, `modified`, and `title` are not
    kept.

`get_token(sandbox: bool) -> Result<String, Error>`

:   As described in the [CLI](cli.qmd) page, this gets the token from either the
    keyring or from the env variables.

`Session {header, url, connection, zendo_id, deposit}`

:   The struct acts as a container to hold everything necessary for all the
    various functions that it is used by. It contains the information needed to
    connect to Zenodo, to send a request, as well as the details from the
    request. This object is used with
    [reqwest](https://docs.rs/reqwest/latest/reqwest/) to build and send the
    request to the [Zenodo API](https://developers.zenodo.org/?shell#rest-api).
    Since `zen-do` doesn't send many requests to Zenodo and because the requests
    are fairly simple, they are sent synchronously. That way we don't need to
    set up any `async` structures. The `connection` field will hold the
    `reqwest::blocking::Client::new()` object, where `blocking` is what sets the
    synchronous connection. The fields `zendo_id` and `deposit` are `Option`
    types.

### `Session::add_files()` {#lib-add-files}

The signature is:

```rust
impl Session {
    pub fn add_files(self: &self, files: NonEmptyVec<&Path>) -> Result<Self, Error>
}
```

Adds files to a Zenodo deposit by sending a `POST` request. Must have the
`"submitted"` field be false (i.e. is unsubmitted). Needs one API call per file.

### `Session::create_new_version()` {#lib-create-new-version}

The signature is:

```rust
impl Session {
    pub fn create_new_version(self: &mut self) -> Result<&mut Self, Error>
}
```

This converts an existing deposit into a ["new
version"](https://developers.zenodo.org/#new-version). It is needed if new files
are going to be added to the deposit. Sends a post request and then needs to
take the response and add it to the `Session.deposit` field.

### `Session::create_deposit()` {#lib-create-deposit}

The signature is:

```rust
impl Session {
    pub fn create_deposit(self: &mut self, metadata: &Metadata) -> Result<&mut Self, Error>`
}
```

This method on creates a new deposit from the `Metadata` in the Zenodo TOML file
by sending a `POST` request to Zenodo. Will add the `deposit` details from the
Zenodo API response.

### `Session::delete_files()` {#lib-delete-files}

The signature is:

```rust
impl Session {
    pub fn delete_files(self: &mut self) -> Result<&mut Self, Error>
}
```

This deletes all files in a deposit by sending delete requests to Zenodo. Gets
the list of files from the `Session.deposit.` fields. Needs one API call per
file.

### `Session::discard_deposit()` {#lib-discard-deposit}

The signature is:

```rust
impl Session {
    pub fn discard_deposit(self: mut self) -> Result<mut self, Error>
}
```

This method sends a [discard](https://developers.zenodo.org/?shell#discard)
request to Zenodo. If the request succeeds, the `Session.deposit` field is set
to `None`. If the current deposit on Zenodo needs to be retrieved, do
`Session::new()` again to start over.

### `Session::get_deposit()` {#lib-get-deposit}

The signature is:

```rust
impl Session {
    fn get_deposit(mut self, id: &ZendoId) -> Result<Self, Error> {}
}
```

Sends a [`GET` REST API request](https://developers.zenodo.org/#list) to Zenodo
using [reqwest](https://docs.rs/reqwest/latest/reqwest/) for any deposit
matching the `ZendoId`, including draft deposits. Deserialises the Zenodo JSON
response into our `Deposit` struct. Uses the Zenodo API `q` query parameter on
the Zenodo `GET` API to list deposits that have the `ZendoId` in the
[`related_identifier`](inputs.qmd#sec-zendo-id) field. If no deposit is found,
the `Session.deposit` field will be kept as `None`. If multiple deposits are
found, it will fail. This is used internally in `Session::new()`, described
[below](#lib-session-new).

### `Session::is_draft()` {#lib-is-draft}

<!-- TODO: Unsure if this should be a `Result` type instead... -->

The signature is:

```rust
impl Session {
    pub fn is_draft(self: &self) -> bool
}
```

Checks the
[`Session.deposit.state`](https://developers.zenodo.org/?shell#representation)
field if it is "inprogress", or if the `state` is not "error" and the
`Session.deposit.submitted` field is false.

### `Session::publish_deposit()` {#lib-publish-deposit}

The signature is:

```rust
impl Session {
    pub fn publish_deposit(self: &self) -> Result<(), Error>
}
```

This method sends a [publish](https://developers.zenodo.org/?shell#publish)
request to Zenodo on the deposit. Returns nothing to indicate the end of the
pipeline.

### `Session::update_deposit()` {#lib-update-deposit}

The signature is:

```rust
impl Session {
    pub fn update_deposit(self: &mut self, metadata: &Metadata) -> Result<&mut Self, Error>
}
```

This method takes the `Metadata` from the Zenodo TOML file and sends an update
request to Zenodo. The response from Zenodo contains the `Deposit`, which will
be added to `Session.deposit` to keep those states between the current session
and the Zenodo server aligned.

### `Session::list_deposits()` {#lib-list-deposit}

The signature is:

```rust
impl Session {
    list_deposits(self: &self) -> Result<Vec<Deposit>, Error>
}
```

Sends a [`get` REST API request](https://developers.zenodo.org/#list) to Zenodo
using the `reqwest` package. Deserialises the Zenodo JSON response into a vector
with our `Deposit` struct. Implemented as an `impl` method on `Session`. Outputs
an empty `Vec` if no deposit is found. Gets all deposits, both draft and
published for the user's Zenodo account, authenticated by their token. While the
Zenodo API includes "page size", we return all deposits without a size
constraint. That's because in our use-case we don't have a large number of
deposits to manage (likely <100), nor do the majority of accounts contain such
large number of deposits that this would be an issue (from what we've seen).

### `Session::new()` {#lib-session-new}

The signature is:

```rust
impl Session {
    new(sandbox: bool, token: String, zendo_id: Option<ZendoId>) -> Result<Self, Error>
}
```

This constructs a new `Session` struct with details needed for `reqwest` to
correctly send a request to Zenodo. Based on the `sandbox` value, the
`Session.url` field will point to either `sandbox.zenodo.org` or `zenodo.org`
URLs. If the `zendo_id` is given, a request will be sent to Zenodo for the
deposit connected to the ID using [`Session::get_deposit()`](#lib-get-deposit),
the response of which will be attached to the `Session.deposit` field to limit
repeated requests. Importantly, the main purpose for getting and assigning the
`Session.deposit` at this point is to get the Zenodo identifier in
[`deposit.id`](https://developers.zenodo.org/?shell#entities). When using
`new()`, the `reqwest::blocking::Client::new()` will be added to
`Session.connection` to reuse that object for each request sent to Zenodo. The
`token` will be added to the header, which will be added to the `reqwest`
connection field.

`trait left_join(self, right: Option<Self>) -> Self`

:   This trait will be used to create methods on all of the different format
    structs. This allows a variety of formats (e.g. `CitationCff`) to be used
    without writing new code for each of those formats. Left join means that all
    the fields in the left hand side (`self`) are kept and any that are missing
    from the right hand side (`right`) are merged into it. This enables any
    values added to an existing file, e.g. `CITATION.cff`, to be kept when
    joined over. If nothing exists on the right side, the left side is output
    without any changes.

`trait const PATH: &Path`

:   This [associated
    constant](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/associated-items.html)
    as a trait applied to the different format structs is used internally in
    `read()` and `write()` to point to the correct locations of the output
    format types. For example, with the enum `ToFormat::CitationCff`, the path
    to this file should be `CITATION.cff`, in the same folder as where the
    `metadata_path` is found.

`trait read() -> Result<Option<Self>, Error>`

:   Like `left_join()` above, this trait as an `impl` method on the format
    structs reads any existing file that is present. If no file is present, it
    will output `None`. Uses the `PATH` const to read the right path location.

`trait write(self) -> Result<(), Error>`

:   Like `left_join()` and `read()` above, this trait as an `impl` method on the
    format structs writes the format to any file. It uses the `PATH` const. It
    will overwrite the contents of the file, though with `left_join()` it will
    maintain any details not found in the `Metadata`.

`ZendoId`

:   This type contains the `zendo_id` value from the Zenodo TOML file, e.g.
    `.zenodo.toml`.
